tasks.notes: fleet/janitor.mjs: `writeDeath` checks the exit code of the status.json PUT but not the journal PUT. `ghPut(exec, contentsPath(target, run, 'janitor-journal.txt'), …)` is awaited and its result discarded, so a failed journal write still yields a death entry with `applied: true` — the entry claims the record the Claim describes ("the unit's result and the journal tail beside it") was written when only half of it was. Concrete case: a prior pass wrote `janitor-journal.txt` and then died before the status PUT; the next pass re-probes the still-live page, PUTs the journal with no `sha=` (correct for a new file, a 422 for an existing one), the journal silently stays stale, the status PUT succeeds, and the run's record is marked `applied: true` against a journal from the earlier probe. M3 does not pin this and leg (c) only exercises the success path, so it is advisory rather than blocking.; fleet/janitor.mjs, header docblock: the surviving BASE sentence "`--dry-run` issues every read and no `rm`." is no longer accurate — under `--dry-run` `writeDeath` returns before `onVm(exec, row.sshDest, journalCommand(run))`, so the journal read is one read a dry pass does not issue (deliberately, and permitted by the task: "the journal read may be skipped under `--dry-run`"). The new prose added above it documents the unit read and the writes but not this exception, so the file's own contract paragraph now overstates what a dry pass does. Suggested wording: "`--dry-run` issues every read but the journal — a death it would write is reported, not written — and no `rm`."; Test-quality nit in `fleet/tests/test_janitor.mjs`: `LIVE_DESTS` is a module-level `Set` mutated by `evidenceFor` and accumulated across every leg, but the leg-(c) loop checks each exec's `exec.vm()` entries against that single global set. A destination that belonged to a live row in one leg is therefore accepted as a live destination in every later leg, so the pin "every ssh <ssh_dest> goes to the ssh_dest of a row whose page said booting|running|publishing" is weaker than it reads — it only fails if a dest was never live in *any* leg. It happens to hold today because each leg uses distinct run numbers, so the exam is not vacuous (LEG_A carries live runs 6, 10 and 11 and does produce `exec.vm()` entries), and `test_janitor_liveness.mjs` leg (a) pins the exact per-leg set with a `deepEqual`, so no criterion is left unverified. Fix, if you want the cross-leg pin to be exact: have `newExec` (or each leg) record its own live-dest set alongside the exec — e.g. `const newExec = (rules, live = new Set()) => { const exec = makeExec({ rules, passthrough: [] }); exec.liveDests = live; EXECS.push(exec); return exec }` with `evidenceFor` returning the live dests it collected — and assert `exec.liveDests.has(call.dest)` in the leg-(c) loop.; concern: Footprint is exactly fleet/janitor.mjs and fleet/tests/test_janitor.mjs; the Proof's test path fleet/tests/test_janitor_liveness.mjs was left for the peer's exam, so it does not exist in this tree and the suite here does not yet exercise it. All six machine clauses were checked against a scratch replica of that exam, written outside the working tree and deleted before the commit.; concern: judgment-call: a unit is parsed to the properties `systemctl show` actually printed, as strings — so the row whose canned answer carries no SubState yields `unit` with three keys, not four with a null. This is the literal reading of "as read"; if the peer's exam cans an empty `SubState=` line the parse still matches (SubState: ''), but a peer expecting numeric ExecMainStatus would not.; concern: doc-lag: fleet/RUNBOOK.md:194 still says the janitor "never sshes into a VM", and fleet/CONTRACT.md's janitor bullet still describes reads only. GLOBAL CONSTRAINTS pin the runbook and the contract byte-identical to BASE, so I left both untouched; CLAUDE.md:86 has the same lag and is outside this task's scope.

completenessFindings.detail: Task 1 (Claim / Context) — `fleet/janitor.mjs:257-261`: `writeDeath` awaits the journal `ghPut` to `.ultrapowers/runs/<N>/janitor-journal.txt` but discards its result, so a non-zero exit on that PUT is silently swallowed. The `deaths` entry's `applied` flag (and the `error` cell on it) reflects only the status.json PUT at `fleet/janitor.mjs:264-271`. If the journal write fails — most concretely on a second death pass for the same run, where the file already exists and the deliberately `sha`-less PUT is a 422 (the omission is correct per the Context's contents-API rule and pinned by Proof leg (c)/M3) — the record transitions to `failed` and `renderJanitor` prints `death <vm> ... ultra/evidence-run-<N>` with no journal beside it and no signal to the operator. This is narrower than it sounds (on a retry the first pass's journal is already on the branch, so the Claim's "journal tail beside it" still holds in the realistic case), and the Machine restatement M3 requires only that the PUT be issued, which it is — hence minor, not blocking. The Context's sentence "A non-zero exit from a PUT ... is recorded on the `deaths` entry as `applied: false` with the output under `error`" is honoured for the status PUT only.
